text:
maria: Seeing a 15-30% p95 spike in the adaptive batcher after the 'kv-prefetch fix' merge (commit abc1234). I ran identical loadgen before/after and attached nsys + perfetto. Anyone available to help bisect?

perf-bot: Autoprofile summary attached: delta in kernel selection and launch patterns. p95 tokens/sec down ~18%. Artifacts uploaded: /tmp/nsys_before.qdrep, /tmp/nsys_after.qdrep :eyes:

aj: Do we have the same harness and same seed for loadgen?

maria: yes — run command was `./tools/loadgen --seq-len-dist=prod --concurrency=12 --seed=2026` for both. Only difference was the merge of abc1234. Topline hotspots below.

maria: ```
Before:  cumulative time -> grouped GEMM kernels (single large launches)
After:   many more small kernel launches; fallback to pointwise_softmax_fast used in ~40% of softmaxs
KV cache hit rate: 96% -> 88%
Batching: average batch size 10.8 -> 7.1 (same concurrency)
```

sam: That KV hit drop could explain smaller batches — if prefetching evicts entries too aggressively we lose prefix cache and batching collapses. Did the change touch eviction windows or KV touch timestamps?

zane: I can bisect. Plan: `git bisect start HEAD abc1234^` then run a lightweight nsys capture and a quick batch-size/hotspot scraper to avoid full long runs. I'll script it.

perf-bot: Bisect job queued (id=42). Estimated runtime 5-8 hours depending on rebuilds.

maria: If bisect hits a commit that changes the batching heuristic, we should capture both nsys and perfetto UI diffs. Perfetto diff links help explain kernel timeline shifts to folks.

zane: Update: bisect pinned bad commit def5678 — it changed `batch_merge_threshold` from 50 -> 30 and added a small optimization around early-kv-prefetch scheduling. Repro locally with minimal harness.

zane: nvprof excerpt: ```
% Time  CPU Time  GPU Time  Name
33.2   1200ms    4800ms    pointwise_softmax_fast
22.1    800ms    3200ms    small_gemm_kernel
10.5    380ms    1500ms    kv_prefetch_kernel
```

aj: That lines up — lowering merge threshold increases number of batches, which affects kernel selector heuristics (more small-size codepaths). The selector prefers a different softmax kernel for small batches.

maria: Two suggested remediations: revert threshold change OR make threshold adaptive based on observed KV hit rate / seq-dist. Also add a safety: if avg_batch_size < X and kv_hit_rate < Y, force the old kernel path.

sam: I'll prototype a conditional: keep `batch_merge_threshold` at 50 when kv_hit_rate >= 0.9. Quick local numbers: baseline p95=220ms, after def5678 p95=270ms, prototype fix p95 ~225ms. I'll push a PR with nsys snapshots and perfetto diffs.

maria: Great — include kernel timeline screenshots and the `nsys` command you ran so reviewers can reproduce. Example: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run_after -t cuda,osrt --sample=cpu -w true --force-overwrite -- ./bin/eng_runtime_test --scenario=prod`

zane: Also added a unit/regression test that simulates high kv hit rate with sparse eviction to prevent future regressions.

aj: Nice. Once PR is up, let's gate it with a perf check step in CI: run a 5-min harness and compare p95 and avg batch size. If >10% regression, fail.

maria: Thanks all! Tagging infra to roll the bisect artifacts into the incident board: https://perf.redwood.local/bisect/42 and adding to the rollout notes. :+1:

perf-bot: Artifact summary saved to ticket PERF-423.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/712 — includes nsys qdrep, perfetto proto, and benchmark script.

maria: I'll review and merge after CI perf gate. Also note to update the kernel selection doc to mention this threshold interplay with KV hit rate.

zane: Follow-up action: add telemetry for `avg_batch_size`, `kv_hit_rate`, and `softmax_kernel_variant` to the console dashboard so we can alert on sudden shifts.

maria: Agreed. Moving this to the eng-runtime oncall checklist once merged. Thanks everyone.
